description:
## Goal

Make the Kernel runtime boundary an ordinary, truthful, private foreign-function boundary.

Public fz wrappers call private foreign declarations. The declaration names the physical runtime export, owns the ABI and semantic contract, and ordinary callable resolution carries its FunctionId. There is no intrinsic registry, synthetic terminal source, name interception, pseudo-extern, or second semantic contract.

## Settled model

- The grammar accepts only `extern "C" defp ...` and `extern "fz" defp ...`. `extern ... def` is rejected until a deliberate public-FFI policy exists.
- Both ABIs call physical C exports. `"C"` passes exactly declared arguments. `"fz"` generically prepends the current `Process*` and uses fz representation lanes.
- Declaration name and physical export name match. Rename `fz_send_ref`, `fz_self_raw`, `fz_make_ref_raw`, `fz_spawn_ref`, and `fz_make_resource_ref` to their declaration names; delete `fz_spawn_opt_ref`.
- Kernel wrappers and private gateways are distinct functions. Retain public wrapper specs and docs. Private externs never enter ModuleInterface.
- Typed builtin identities own pid, ref, and cpointer. The generic ABI mapper may select their physical lanes but never recovers semantics from rendered type strings.
- `spawn/1` remains an ordinary `"fz"` private extern plus Kernel wrapper. Delete the inert fz-only `spawn/2` and every spawn_opt path. Do not add other spawn forms here.
- A linker name is legitimate physical ABI data only. It is never semantic authority, a type identity, effect policy, or post-resolution dispatch key.

## Strategy

First make private extern visibility an ordinary source property. Then rename runtime exports and route every retained Kernel foreign call through generic `ExternAbi::C` or `ExternAbi::Fz` lowering in every door. Remove string-keyed interceptors, aliases, and duplicate semantic ABI tables.

Inventory every context-free `"C"` declaration. A retained declaration must name a real C export and use the generic path. If an apparent extern is actually a language operator, locate its existing language or IR authority rather than preserve a fake extern or add a new intrinsic subsystem.

A private foreign callable follows ordinary private callable rules, including existing function-value behavior. Test direct calls and private capture through an ordinary higher-order call. Do not invent public foreign callable behavior; public declaration syntax remains rejected.

## Acceptance

- Kernel internal gateways are `extern ... defp`, absent from ModuleInterface, and callable only through ordinary lexical resolution.
- `extern "C"` adds no process parameter. `extern "fz"` adds exactly one current Process parameter and uses one generic typed marshalling path in interpreter, JIT, and AOT.
- Every renamed runtime entry has the same declaration and physical export name. No _raw/_ref alias, symbol-name interception, pseudo-extern, or duplicate ABI authority remains.
- pid, ref, and cpointer remain typed semantic identities while generic ABI lowering uses correct physical lanes.
- send, self, spawn/1, make_ref, make_resource, and panic agree across all execution doors through ordinary extern lowering.
- spawn/2 and all spawn_opt code, hooks, symbols, tests, fixtures, and documentation are absent without a compatibility shim.
- Context-free foreign calls are real generic C calls or are moved to their existing non-FFI authority after evidence.
- Unchanged requests reuse products; unrelated edits do not cause runtime-boundary work. Tests inspect typed facts and deterministic telemetry.
- Focused, library, fixture, CLI, check, strict Clippy, format, deterministic reuse, and artifact gates pass. Documentation describes only this final model.
- No rejected descriptor/terminal scaffolding, probe, adapter, compatibility path, stale test, or obsolete documentation remains.

## Causality

fz-tfn.69 is complete. This ticket no longer provides a hidden terminal identity to fz-tfn.62; remove any dependency based on that rejected premise and audit the remaining graph for real ordering only.

## Review

A fresh ticket-scoped cold review must verify source visibility, ABI truthfulness, exact physical names, elimination of symbol-keyed special cases, typed lane selection, all-door behavior, spawn_opt deletion, reuse telemetry, documentation, and the one-ticket PR boundary before commit and close.
title: Make Kernel runtime calls ordinary private foreign declarations
